rubricDispositions.rationale: User-visible connection selection remains scoped to an active admin organization and connect completion checks tenant/provider organization equality. Directory writes load one providerConnection by connectionKey, propagate that row's organizationKey into sourceChannels/channelSyncStates, filter existing channel rows by connectionKey, and reject duplicate Slack team/app/bot bindings even when the duplicate belongs to another agency.

S04-T02 adds only internal Slack directory query/mutation/action functions; public authorization for creating/completing the Slack connection is still enforced by the existing Slack connection layer with requireAdmin and tenant checks before any connectionKey can enter the directory workflow.

Identity replacement paths revoke the provider connection, mark source channels access_lost, clear leases, pause all live/recent/deep/reconciliation lanes, and attach replacement audit state. Documentation records additive rollback behavior and states no provider tokens/raw Slack credentials are stored in the new rows.

The new provider interface accepts only opaque connection identifiers, provider exceptions are normalized to typed errors, the default implementation fails closed, and the changed directory code contains no secret/env access or logging of raw provider payloads. Durable rows store Slack team/app/bot/channel metadata and explicitly avoid provider tokens or raw credentials.

Every commit mutation reloads the connection and revalidates expectedGeneration before applying identity/channel changes, duplicate or replacement races return a controlled bot-identity mismatch path with revocation/audit, and stale-generation race tests prove mismatched generations cannot commit.

Channel reconciliation is upsert-based using connectionKey plus externalChannelId/channelKey, preserves firstDiscoveredAt and existing live lane cursor/lease fields on replay, and the replay test verifies repeated page reconciliation does not create duplicate channel rows.

expectedGeneration fences reads and commits before provider calls; same-connection reauthorization increments the generation while promoting all old channel and sync rows to preserve keys/cursors; tests cover stale-generation provider-call suppression and partial-page reauthorization cursor preservation.

Slack provider access is isolated behind SlackDirectoryProviderService and limited to auth.test plus conversations.list. The planning/test evidence asserts conversations.join is not called, and provider rate limiting remains a typed ProviderRateLimited error rather than being swallowed or leaking raw provider details.
